leading_positions.synthesis: Five of the eight round-1 files put optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) as the single preferred prize part. All five give the same two laureates and describe the same division of credit: Katori for the magic-wavelength proposal and first demonstrations, Ye for the accuracy, stability and many-body programme. Their citations are close but not identical; several ask that it name the magic-wavelength lattice so it is not read as a second frequency-comb prize. Shared reservations are novelty relative to the 2005 (comb) and 2012 (ion control) prizes, possible priority claims of Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Oates and others who are outside the supplied names, and the fact that the redefinition of the second has not yet happened. What is not shared is the weight put on each: some treat these as caveats, others as questions needing a check of the record before the final ballot. Two of the five (Olsson, Pearce) moved to B031 after reading the opening ballots, Olsson from B009 and Pearce from B005.

Two members prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, with the same three names (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer). Both cite a continuum-model prediction followed by an unexpected experimental discovery that many groups have reproduced. Both name B031 as an alternative and concede that maturity (unsettled pairing mechanism, under a decade of experiments) and the absence of the first experimental author of the 2018 papers are real weaknesses. Mehlig now includes Bistritzer, having moved from the two-name set in his opening after Eriksson's attribution argument, and both want the citation built around flat bands and correlated states and not a mechanism for superconductivity. Their disagreement with the B031 camp is mainly about whether the pairing question is a maturity problem or a detail, and whether the clock counts as a new discovery.

One member prefers the Higgs boson discovery with ATLAS and CMS (Gianotti, Jenni, Della Negra), arguing that it is the most fundamental and best-confirmed result on the shortlist and the unrecognised experimental half of the 2013 prize. He names B031 and B024 as alternatives and accepts that the attribution is the main difficulty. Others, including me, say the science is beyond dispute but do not make B005 a preferred configuration because three names cannot be defended as a stable allocation. I moved from B005 to B031 in my own file but keep B005 as my first alternative.

areas_of_agreement: Katori and Ye are accepted by every member who discusses B031 as the natural pair, and members of both the B031 and B024 camps name B031 as an alternative or a safe fallback; no member argues against its scientific standing.

The Higgs discovery is acknowledged as scientifically first-rate and mature by members who do not prefer it (Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Johansson); the objection raised is attribution, not merit.

The pairing mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is unsettled and the first experimental author of the 2018 papers is outside the credited names; Eriksson and Mehlig acknowledge both points in their own files.

B028 (Hubbard-model simulation) is treated as a strong idea but its five credited names do not reduce to three without a contested theory/experiment split; Lindroth, Johansson, Olsson and Mehlig each say so in their files.
Members agree the Krivanek (STEM corrector) priority question weakens B009 as presently credited, including its first-place proposer Olsson, who no longer prefers it.
scientific_disputes: Whether lattice clocks are a distinct physical idea (many neutral atoms interrogated at the magic wavelength, bringing stability and many-body effects) or an incremental refinement of optical frequency standards already recognised in 2005 and 2012; Mehlig weighs the novelty question against B031 while Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce argue it is distinct.

Whether the discovery in B024 is the existence of flat bands and correlated insulating and superconducting states (Eriksson, Mehlig) or whether an unexplained superconducting phase makes the discovery incomplete (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth).

Whether an enabling instrument or measurement technique counts as a physics discovery for the purposes of the prize: raised for B009 by Eriksson, Olsson and Johansson, and by Olsson and Mehlig for B031's metrology character, with the answer tied to the fundamental-physics return (redshift tests, constants, dark matter).
attribution_disputes: B005: committee members proposed different trios drawn from Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee. The open choice is between founding leaders of the projects and spokespeople at the time of discovery, and it decides whether Gianotti or Virdee is dropped. Kroll and Lindroth say the lack of a principled rule is why they do not prefer B005.

B031: whether Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Oates, Hinkley and others have priority claims that should alter a two-name prize. Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson, Johansson and I all say we cannot verify this from the files; Lindroth asks for a check before the final ballot.

B024: Bistritzer is included by Eriksson and Mehlig as co-author of the 2011 continuum-model calculation; Olsson and Pearce regard the missing experimental first author as outside any three-name credit, and nobody has proposed a way to include them.

B028: allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger, Zoller and Cirac (with Jaksch not on the list); Mehlig's earlier trio used Esslinger in place of Zoller, which differs from the Bloch, Greiner, Zoller trio of other members.
B009: Krivanek, Dellby and Batson developed the STEM corrector in parallel with the TEM correctors of Haider, Rose and Urban, so the three supplied names may not capture the decisive credit.
maturity_disputes: B024 is about eight years old since the 2018 experiments. Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth call it premature; Eriksson and Mehlig say independent replication across groups and platforms is stronger than at the time of some earlier prizes.

B031 is reproduced at the 10^-18 level by several independent laboratories and is called mature by all who discuss it, but the formal redefinition of the second and applications such as geodesy and dark-matter searches are still prospective; Johansson and Kroll ask whether to wait for the redefinition.
B040 (IceCube): I raise the question of whether source identification has matured beyond the established diffuse flux; no other member makes it their preferred configuration.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson discloses a possible connection to B016 (circuit QED) through WACQT and Chalmers colleagues and says he will recuse or defer on B016 if the committee moves toward it.

Kroll notes that his WACQT role overlaps institutionally with Chalmers on B016 and discloses a distant mentor-network tie to John Hall's laboratory (JILA tradition behind Ye's group), not regarded by him as requiring recusal.

Olsson says B009 lies directly in her own field and in the community she presides over (IFSM) and she would recuse or declare the connection; she also notes a Fellow link with the University of Tokyo (Katori's institution) that she does not regard as a conflict.

Lindroth discloses close collaboration with Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and notes that proximity to the atomic-physics community of B031 and B028 should be recorded; no credited B031 name is a collaborator.
Eriksson notes that he chaired the 2025 committee, which bears on the timing of B016 but does not require recusal in his view.

I (Pearce) note close familiarity as an astroparticle physicist with the IceCube field (B040) and a general CERN-community link to B005, and I would take extra care before pressing B040 beyond alternative status; I am not in ATLAS, CMS or IceCube.
questions_for_round2: B031: What is the decisive physical step that separates the lattice clock from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, and can a citation that names magic-wavelength trapping express it? Mehlig, who ranks B031 eighth, is asked to say whether novelty is his only objection and whether he could accept B031 as a second choice.
B031: Can the priority record of Katori, Ye, Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Oates and Hinkley be checked before the final ballot, and does it support limiting the prize to two names?

B024: Is the unresolved pairing mechanism a maturity problem or only a detail of one phase, and does the committee want to wait for further independent replication? Is there any way to represent the first experimental author of the 2018 papers within three laureates, and should the citation avoid claiming a mechanism?

B005: Should attribution follow founding leadership or spokespeople at the time of the 2012 discovery, and can members who do not prefer B005 state a rule that would let it be defended with three names, or is the three-person limit disqualifying this year?

Single or multi-part: do any members want a second prize part alongside the leading choice (for example B009 or B028), given that Olsson notes that a B031 plus B009 pair would need five names under the three-person limit?
B009 and instruments: if instrument inventions are eligible, what separates B009 and B031 as physics discoveries, and does the Krivanek priority question rule B009 out as currently credited?
Timing and balance: how much should the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits and the 2023, 2012 and 2005 prizes in atomic and optical physics weigh against candidates from the same area this year?
summary.chair_observation: On the explicit round-1 positions, five of eight members prefer B031, two prefer B024 and one prefers B005; I am among the five and moved from B005 in my own file. B031 draws support from members of different specialities and has the most settled attribution, but its remaining questions (distinctness from earlier prizes, priority outside Katori and Ye) are untested in discussion. B024 and B005 each rest on strong science and contested attribution or maturity, and are not yet reconciled with the B031 camp. Round 2 should settle the distinctness and priority checks for B031 and test whether the B024 and B005 concerns can be met.
